name: Ossification of the Posterior Longitudinal Ligament
definition: Pathological ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament, most commonly in the cervical spine, which can narrow the canal and cause myelopathy or radiculopathy.

investigations.principle: Clinical and imaging correlation is essential.
investigations.MRI: MRI assesses cord compression and cord signal change; CT best demonstrates ossification morphology.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may suggest OPLL but CT is more definitive.

amber: Progressive or moderate/severe myelopathy generally requires surgical assessment; high-risk cervical manipulation should be avoided.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vata-neurological phenotype may be documented only in parallel; OPLL remains a modern structural diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Pathological ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament, most commonly in the cervical spine, which can narrow the canal and cause myelopathy or radiculopathy.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
